items.title: Every U.S. State Ranks Above Every Foreign Economy in Household Consumption
items.raw:
评论 49824328: Interesting chart, but how is consumption measured? Dollars or stuff? Everything costs way more in the US.
评论 49824905: Measured in overpriced US dollars. No one would willingly live in Mississippi over France or Italy. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Lasker
评论 49825009: This seems to be about actual consumption that has not been adjusted for government subsidies. If country A subsidizes services such as education, childcare, and healthcare more than country B, household spending is going to be lower there. A better comparison would either ignore spending in commonly subsidized categories or include government subsidies in household spending. A quick reality check: Norway would be one of the wealthiest US states, both by nominal figures and after adjusting for purchasing power. If your comparison says something else, you are probably doing something wrong.

analysis.title_zh: ArXiv 获多年资助，将以独立非营利组织运营
analysis.strategy: 围绕“AI 生成论文洪流下的可信度筛查”做信息甄别层，而非自建论文库
analysis.reason: 讨论中出现两个可核查的痛点信号：一是 arXiv 主编层面自述难以跟上 AI 生成论文的涌入，二是读者对单作者新账号论文默认当作低质。但当前证据只到抱怨与新闻层面，没有任何付费行为、采购决策或既有付费替代品的证据，因此不能判定有市场，只适合继续观察。

facts.quote: Tom Dietterich (Editor in Chief at arXiv) posted on LinkedIn the other day that they’re having trouble keeping up with the onslaught of AI-generated papers. Lots of suggestions in the comments but no magic bullets.
facts.translation_zh: arXiv 主编 Tom Dietterich 前几天在领英上发帖说，他们难以跟上 AI 生成论文的洪流。评论区有很多建议，但都没有万能解法。

facts.quote: Personally if I see a single author post 2023, I assume it’s junk, especially if they’re not from an actual research institution.
facts.translation_zh: 就我个人而言，如果看到一篇 2023 年之后发表的单作者论文，我会默认它是垃圾，尤其当作者并非来自真正的研究机构时更是如此。

unknowns: 谁真正愿意为论文可信度筛查付费：读者、编辑、机构还是图书馆
是否已有成熟服务在做同类筛查且已被采用
单篇筛查的人工成本与可自动化程度
arXiv 自身或其资助方是否会直接内置此类功能
analysis.user: 待验证：可能是需要快速筛选文献的研究生、审稿人、期刊编辑或科研机构的文献管理人员。
analysis.task: 待验证：在阅读前判断一篇预印本是否值得读、是否来自真实研究机构、是否疑似 AI 批量生成。
analysis.current_solution: 待验证：靠个人经验规则（如看作者数量、发表年份、所属机构）以及 OpenReview 等平台的人工评审。
analysis.gap: 待验证：现有做法依赖个人经验，且评论指出部分评审人也在使用大模型或几乎不认真读稿，筛查环节本身不可靠。
analysis.mvp: 候选形态：输入一个 arXiv 链接或作者列表，输出该论文的可核查信号清单（作者机构真实性、发表节奏异常、是否疑似批量生成、引用与内容一致性），只做提示不做好坏判定；先以人工复核的方式跑通几十篇样本，验证输出是否比个人经验规则更有用。
analysis.distribution: 候选路径：在 arXiv、OpenReview、科研社区的相关讨论帖中给出样本报告，或与实验室、期刊编辑做小范围试用；先验证再谈规模化。
analysis.monetization: 未知，暂不建议按订阅定价；需先确认是个人自付还是机构采购。
analysis.fit: 部分匹配：轻量网站形态可行，但需要一定的科研领域知识与数据核查能力，个人/小团队能否稳定获取并判断信号尚待核实。
analysis.next_step: 先查清三件事：arXiv 是否已公开任何质量筛查机制；是否有现成工具覆盖该任务；以及找 3 至 5 位真实读者确认他们当前如何判断论文可信度、是否会为此付出时间或金钱。在得到这些答案前不要开工。
analysis.risk: 误判成本高，把正常论文标为可疑会伤害研究者声誉；同时该需求可能由平台自身或免费社区工具解决，个人产品难以建立付费理由。

items.title: We just shipped support for the ugliest part of HTTP: Vary
items.raw:
评论 49823961: I've been wanting this from Cloudflare for years . The classic problem here is if you do that thing where user agents that send "accept: text/html" get HTML, while user agents that don't get JSON or some other format. This used to be impossible to deploy behind Cloudflare caching, because they ignored the Vary header on anything other than images - so you risked caching the JSON version and then serving it up to someone who was expecting HTML. (Independent of the Cloudflare feature I ended up deciding never to use that pattern, because I prefer having URL that predictably returns HTML or JSON - I add a .json suffix to my apps to serve JSON instead.)
评论 49823965: Nice to see. I’ve used vary to quite a bit of success on CloudFront back in the day. I actually assumed when I started using Cloudflare that it did have vary support and it led to a serious bug in my sass app at the time.
评论 49824063: I honestly thought they would never ship this. Holy hell this has been a long time coming. Actual real content negotiation in 2026. Never thought I'd live to see the day.
评论 49824234: "If the origin response does not include a Vary header, Cloudflare caches the response normally"[1] "If one response omits it, Cloudflare could cache that response without the variance needed to keep it isolated."[2] Will that non-Vary cache object front-run any Vary-segmented cache objects? If so, probably worth adding a snippet rule to ensure every response has a Vary header? 1: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/vary/#how-v... 2: https://blog.cloudflare.com/vary-support/#how-a-response-mov...
评论 49824618: finally. now maybe they'll have time to implement a working unsubscribe on their marketing emails.

analysis.title_zh: 我们刚刚支持了HTTP中最丑陋的部分：Vary
analysis.strategy: 服务产品化：把Vary/内容协商的缓存验证做成轻量测试与回归工具。
analysis.reason: 评论显示开发者长期因CDN忽略Vary而遭遇JSON/HTML串缓存，属于真实技术痛点；但Cloudflare已补齐核心支持，剩余机会在验证与回归，规模和付费意愿待验证。

facts.quote: This used to be impossible to deploy behind Cloudflare caching, because they ignored the Vary header on anything other than images - so you risked caching the JSON version and then serving it up to someone who was expecting HTML.
facts.translation_zh: 过去在Cloudflare缓存后部署这是不可能的，因为他们除了图片以外忽略Vary头——所以你可能缓存了JSON版本，然后把它提供给期待HTML的人。

facts.quote: I actually assumed when I started using Cloudflare that it did have vary support and it led to a serious bug in my sass app at the time.
facts.translation_zh: 实际上，我开始使用Cloudflare时以为它确实支持Vary，结果当时在我的sass应用里导致了一个严重bug。

unknowns: 多CDN之间的差异
相关搜索需求规模

analysis.user: 使用CDN的Web开发者、小团队和独立开发者
analysis.task: 确认Vary与内容协商是否被CDN正确缓存，避免不同Accept/UA的响应串缓存
analysis.current_solution: 手动curl、查看CDN文档、避免内容协商改用.json后缀、依赖平台修复
analysis.gap: 缺少一键跨Accept/UA的缓存行为检查、诊断和回归告警
analysis.mvp: 输入URL与一组Accept/UA，输出缓存键、响应变体、是否串缓存，并生成可重复的回归测试
analysis.distribution: 开发者SEO、Hacker News、Cloudflare社区、GitHub Action
analysis.monetization: 免费基础检测；团队监控/多CDN回归订阅
analysis.fit: 个人团队可做轻量网站或CLI，但需覆盖多个CDN和缓存环境
analysis.next_step: 先收集“Vary缓存错误”相关搜索词与论坛帖，访谈5位使用Cloudflare的开发者
analysis.risk: 平台继续内建功能、付费意愿低、测试环境复杂、误报

Interviews with these bookstores reveal reports of "100 books sold per day" and "days where sales have increased fivefold," leading to widespread speculation within the industry that the orders are intended to collect training data for generative AI (artificial intelligence). Further investigation revealed records of over 50 tons of books being exported from Japan to the United States. Is it acceptable for books to be consumed and discarded for AI training? items.title: VSCode's SSH Agent Is Bananas (2025)
items.raw:
评论 49823004: When I give an agent ssh access to something I want to be able to watch and fully understand what it's doing. I want it to essentially only "type" things into the CLI that I could have typed myself, I can comprehend what it's doing, and am not surprised by the results. Opencode and a smart LLM (qwen 3.8-flash-next, deepseek v4 0731 or smarter) do relatively well with this in my experience.
评论 49823036: Missing a (2025) FYI VSCode's SSH Agent is a godsend for remote development - the "disadvantages" that Fly lists are part of its advantages. I've worked in several teams that have made extensive use of the extension, and it's never been an issue. You can restrict SSH access arbitrarily to ensure whatever security or access guardrails you need.
评论 49823067: > Emacs hosts the spiritual forebearer of remote editing systems, a blob of hyper-useful Elisp called “Tramp”. If you can hook Tramp up to any kind of interactive environment — usually, an SSH session — where it can run Bourne shell commands, it can extend Emacs to that environment. vs. > The agent runs over port-forwarded SSH. It establishes a WebSockets connection back to your running VSCode front-end. The underlying protocol on that connection can: Wander around the filesystem; - Edit arbitrary files; Launch its own shell PTY processes; Persist itself. So... basically the same things that Tramp could do as well? > In security-world, there’s a name for tools that work this way. I won’t say it out loud, because that’s not fair to VSCode, but let’s just say the name is murid in nature. Yeah, it's called RAT, and an ur-example of it is SSH itself (especially when allowed to run a shell remotely), so... not sure why are you freaking out. I mean, I'd probably prefer if VS Code simply ran ed/vim remotely, but both of those editors can invoke shell anyhow so... eh?
评论 49823093: This part of VSCode's architecture is acceptable to me. The reverse direction, where a compromised remote can do whatever it wants to my local machine, is not.
评论 49823167: This extension and devcontainers is basically the way to go for large dev teams inmho

items.title: Show HN: Letter – Relationship-based access control (ReBAC) Postgres extension
items.raw:
评论 49822547: Hi HN, This extension provides relationship-based access control (ReBAC) for PostgreSQL. It's a rewrite of the DDLX permissions system I wrote while working at ElectricSQL, but just for internal use in Postgres rather than for a distributed sync system. It lets you model the kind of permissions you need for complex multi-tenant applications directly inside the DB. This extension is still just a beta and not production ready, it needs bunch more testing so don't use it with anything important yet.

评论 49824099: I listened to this podcast and it was maddening. A few of his frames : AI is just software, nothing new to see here. AI safety is primarily a sandboxing problem. There is no collective action problem, and every company should just slow down if they think they need to slow down. There is no need for regulation because the existing incentives in the market keep companies from acting badly, which is why no company has ever done anything bad. If something bad does happen, then we can regulate after the fact. We will end up creating more jobs than we destroy, so don't worry about it. Our kids might forget a whole bunch of stuff or never learn it in the first place. But don't worry, they'll come up with new things to learn instead. The only way to get safety is to move faster because then we will more quickly arrive at safety. Recursive self-improvement is just what we've always done. The real danger is alarmism that might scare the public and the young people. Nothing bad can happen, it can only good happen.

items.title: Show HN: QBasic 1.1 in the Browser
items.raw:
I built an independent reimplementation of the QBasic 1.1 compiler, virtual machine, and IDE that runs entirely in the browser. TypeScript with a Svelte 5 frontend.
评论 49822337: Looks cool, but unfortunately doesn’t trigger the keyboard on mobile
评论 49823499: Nice job~ For the past 6 months I've also been working on a period-accurate QBASIC 1.1 simulator (and corresponding virtual hardware layer) that runs entirely in the browser. I've got a stack of books on my desk from when I was a kid in the 90s that have literally been my religious texts ( Undocumented DOS, The Programmer's PC Sourcebook, etc ), so I know how hard it is to get this right. I've actually posted about it a couple times here in HN. Anyway small bit of feedback: Technically if you don't clear the screen (using CLS, or set a SCREEN mode other than zero), the cursor retains its position even between program executions. So basically if you have a program like this: PRINT "WHY IS A RAVEN LIKE A WRITING DESK" END And then you run it again - the output screen should display: WHY IS A RAVEN LIKE A WRITING DESK WHY IS A RAVEN LIKE A WRITING DESK There's a thousand other subtleties like this that make the proverbial "last mile" sometimes feel insurmountable. Fun though! * Your definition of "fun" may vary.
